<description>
Currently we have no automation in place to check that our code signing certificates are not expired or close to expiry. We have previously "relied on Release Candidates" as a dry-run for codesigners to realise that a certificate has expired and have time to fix it. "Noticing during RC cycle" also might not be appropriate in the future if we release more bugfix minor/patch releases on short notice.

In place of this process we can run a weekly CI job which will check the certificate's validity and open an issue when it passes an expiry threshold.

In this draft we only check the windows cert (as I couldn't find a mac one) and we set the alert threshold to 90 days.

When the threshold is passed, the job will open an issue in this repo (optionally tagging relevant key-holders).
</description>

<commits>

Check the signing certificate on master weekly so maintainers have time
to renew it before Windows release signing is affected. Open an issue
within 90 days of expiry, including certificate details and the checked
commit.

<patch>
diff --git a/.github/workflows/code-signing-certificate.yml b/.github/workflows/code-signing-certificate.yml
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..7562692ded
--- /dev/null
+++ b/.github/workflows/code-signing-certificate.yml
@@ -0,0 +1,72 @@
+# Copyright (c) 2026-present The Bitcoin Core developers
+# Distributed under the MIT software license, see the accompanying
+# file COPYING or https://opensource.org/license/mit.
+
+name: Code signing certificate
+on:
+  workflow_dispatch:
+  schedule:
+    # Mondays at 09:23 UTC.
+    - cron: '23 9 * * 1'
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+  issues: write
+
+concurrency:
+  group: code-signing-certificate
+
+jobs:
+  check-certificate:
+    if: github.repository == 'bitcoin/bitcoin'
+    runs-on: ubuntu-slim
+    timeout-minutes: 5
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
+        with:
+          ref: master
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      - name: Check certificate expiry
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
+          GH_REPO: bitcoin/bitcoin
+        shell: bash
+        run: |
+          CERT=contrib/windeploy/win-codesign.cert
+          WARNING_DAYS=90
+          # The first certificate in the PEM bundle is the code signing certificate.
+          # Parse it before checking expiry so malformed input fails the job.
+          DETAILS=$(openssl x509 -in "$CERT" -noout -subject -issuer -dates -sha256 -fingerprint)
+          if openssl x509 -in "$CERT" -noout -checkend "$((WARNING_DAYS * 86400))"; then
+            exit 0
+          fi
+
+          EXPIRY=$(openssl x509 -in "$CERT" -noout -enddate)
+          export TITLE="Windows code signing certificate expires ${EXPIRY#notAfter=}"
+          # Include closed issues so closing an alert acknowledges this expiry.
+          EXISTING=$(gh issue list --state all --search "\"$TITLE\" in:title" \
+            --json title,url --jq '.[] | select(.title == env.TITLE) | .url')
+          if [[ -n "$EXISTING" ]]; then
+            echo "Certificate expiry already reported: $EXISTING"
+            exit 0
+          fi
+
+          STATUS="expires within $WARNING_DAYS days"
+          if ! openssl x509 -in "$CERT" -noout -checkend 0; then
+            STATUS="has expired"
+          fi
+          COMMIT=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
+          cat > "$RUNNER_TEMP/certificate-issue.md" <<EOF
+          The Windows code signing certificate $STATUS. Please renew it and update \`$CERT\`.
+
+          Certificate checked on [master at $COMMIT]($GITHUB_SERVER_URL/$GH_REPO/blob/$COMMIT/$CERT):
+
+          \`\`\`text
+          $DETAILS
+          \`\`\`
+
+          Warning threshold: $WARNING_DAYS days before expiry.
+          [Weekly check]($GITHUB_SERVER_URL/$GH_REPO/actions/runs/$GITHUB_RUN_ID).
+          EOF
+          gh issue create --title "$TITLE" --body-file "$RUNNER_TEMP/certificate-issue.md"

</patch>
